svg.title: Stepwise NEST control: overhead, speed and threading
svg.desc: Three panels measured with NEST 3.9.0 on one workstation at NCP commit 2819dae. Panel a: prepared chunked advancement costs 1.45 times one Run call for 1 ms chunks, 1.05 times for 10 ms chunks and 1.007 times for 100 ms chunks, with equal aggregate spike counts. Panel b: biological seconds per wall-clock second for 1, 4 and 8 threads from 2,000 to 20,000 neurons with 500 recurrent inputs per neuron. Panel c: a Python counter retains 1.2 percent of its rate in one probe around nest.Run, and serial-to-threaded period ratios are 0.96 to 1.04.

g.font-family: 'Source Sans Pro', 'Source Sans 3', 'Latin Modern Math', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
g.text: STEPWISE NEST CONTROL · OVERHEAD, SPEED AND THREADING
NEST 3.9.0 on one workstation; NCP benchmark scripts at 2819dae; (a,b) minimum times; (c) one probe and loop pair.
(c) Can Python overlap transport with a running kernel?
1.2% retained in one probe around Run()
Source: rerun of NCP's bench_chunk_overhead.py, bench_realtime.py and bench_overlap.py on 7 October 2026; values are indicative, not calibrated.
